answer: The beacon keeper tends the flame through the whole polar night, and the watch book records the flame's check at every bell. A basalt watch kept from a warm hut fails the beacon: at the wharf of the night the keeper must stand in the wind and read the flame himself, and a hut-kept watch lets the light die unseen. Faking the watch means living at the beacon for a full winter, tending 200 nights of flame and paying 14,900, while the spiral entry in the watch book is countersigned by the harbour master weekly, so a night whose flame was never checked is struck from the record.
